_doc: The yearly tourney. Once the town holds the 'tier' charter, the council proposes it on day 'proposeDay' of the 'season'; the lists open on day 'openDay' of it, one event a day. The mayor funds it at a level (cost = gold x (1 + population / perPeople) + wealth x treasury, purses included) or skips it (mandate and a sulk). Each level sets how many ride in each event (half at most from the town's heroes whose class fits, the rest champions of the neighbouring settlements), the crowd it draws (visitors times 'tourists', each paying 'gate' gold at the lists), the mood on tourney days and the renown the winner and the runner-up earn. An arena (or the Grand Arena institution) makes all of it 'arena.scale' bigger. A heat is the event's rounds, each an opposed d20 + ability modifier + proficiency (half for a class that doesn't fit, and 'home' more for the town's own heroes, cheered on by the crowd); most rounds won takes it, ties ride again on the first round's ability. 'cast' is the class's own casting ability. Betting: one stake an event, at fair odds less the bookmakers' 'edge', before its first heat.

levels.name: Modest
levels.text: A field outside the gate, a rope for a barrier and a barrel of ale for the winners.

levels.name: Grand
levels.text: Painted lists, a stand for the gentry, heralds and a purse worth riding for.

levels.name: Legendary
levels.text: Silk pavilions, minstrels from three realms and a purse that brings champions from every hold in the wilds.

events.name: the Joust
events.blurb: Lances couched, two riders thunder down the tilt. Strength breaks lances; the hardy stay in the saddle.

events.name: the Archery
events.blurb: Three ends at the butts and a last arrow at a peeled willow wand. A steady hand and a calm eye win it.

events.name: the Wizards' Duel
events.blurb: Inside a ring of chalk and wardstones, two casters trade harmless fire until one ward fails. Each casts with their own art.

events.name: the Race
events.blurb: Twice round the walls on foot. Quick feet at the start and finish, wind for the long stretch.
